concept: CCE: 'comprehensive' means scholastic plus co-scholastic coverage
must_teach: In CCE, 'continuous' means regular assessment through the year; 'comprehensive' means covering both scholastic (subjects) and co-scholastic areas (life skills, attitudes, values, arts, sports). It is not about written vs oral or internal vs external.

concept: Project method developed by W. H. Kilpatrick (1918)
must_teach: Kilpatrick set out the project method in 1918 on Dewey's learning by doing; steps purposing, planning, executing, evaluating. Montessori and Froebel are early-childhood educators; Helen Parkhurst devised the Dalton Plan.

concept: Understanding level aims at grasping relationships among facts and principles
must_teach: Understanding level (Morrison) goes beyond rote memory to seeing relationships among facts and generalisations so learners can explain and apply them. Rote recall is memory level; independent problem-solving is reflective level.

concept: Tutorial: small group, tutor attends to individual difficulties
must_teach: A tutorial is a small-group session where a tutor clears doubts and gives personal feedback, supplementing lectures. Lecture addresses a large group; symposium and conference involve formal presentations by several speakers.

concept: Micro-teaching originated at Stanford University (Allen, 1963)
must_teach: Micro-teaching was developed at Stanford University in 1963 by Dwight W. Allen and colleagues for controlled practice of single skills with immediate feedback; later adapted in India.

concept: Revised Bloom (2001) highest level is Create
must_teach: Revised taxonomy order: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create; Create is highest. In the 1956 original, Evaluation was highest with Synthesis below it.

concept: Norm-referenced test compares a score with others' scores
must_teach: Norm-referenced tests interpret a score relative to a group (ranks, percentiles), as in competitive selection. Criterion-referenced tests compare with a fixed standard regardless of others; self-referenced compares with one's own earlier performance.

concept: Zone of Proximal Development given by Vygotsky
must_teach: Vygotsky's ZPD is the gap between what a learner can do alone and with help from a teacher or more capable peer. Piaget (stages), Bruner (modes, discovery) and Ausubel (advance organisers) are distinct.

concept: Reliability means consistency of scores on repeated administration
must_teach: A reliable test gives consistent results on re-administration under similar conditions. Validity asks whether the test measures what it claims to measure; economy/usability concerns practicality.

concept: Andragogy popularised by Malcolm Knowles
must_teach: Malcolm Knowles popularised andragogy, the art and science of helping adults learn; adults are self-directed, experienced, ready to learn for life roles, problem-centred, internally motivated. Pedagogy is teaching children; Piaget, Skinner, Bloom are unrelated.

concept: Lecture is a teacher-centred method
must_teach: In a lecture the teacher controls content and pace while learners listen, so it is teacher-centred; economical for large classes but little learner activity.

concept: Affective domain taxonomy by Krathwohl, Bloom and Masia (1964)
must_teach: Krathwohl, Bloom and Masia published the affective taxonomy in 1964 (Receiving to Characterisation). Simpson and Dave are psychomotor taxonomists; Gagné is known for conditions of learning.

concept: Reflective practice: teacher critically examines own teaching to improve
must_teach: Reflective practice means a teacher looks back on her own teaching, asks what worked and changes future lessons. Subject mastery and verbal fluency describe knowledge or speech, not self-examination.

concept: Diagnostic test locates specific learning difficulties
must_teach: A diagnostic test identifies where and why a learner goes wrong so remedial teaching can follow. Prognostic tests predict future success, aptitude tests measure potential in a field, intelligence tests measure general mental ability.

concept: Large class size limits individual attention
must_teach: As class size grows, individual guidance, interaction and feedback suffer; lectures, announcements and common tests can still be given to large groups.

concept: VARK (Fleming): V stands for Visual
must_teach: Neil Fleming's VARK = Visual, Auditory/Aural, Read/Write, Kinaesthetic; visual learners prefer diagrams, charts and maps.

concept: Brainstorming (Osborn) generates many ideas without early criticism
must_teach: Brainstorming, introduced by Alex Osborn, asks a group to produce as many ideas as possible, deferring criticism/evaluation. It is not for memorising, testing or revising.

concept: Multiple intelligences theory proposed by Howard Gardner (1983)
must_teach: Gardner's Frames of Mind (1983) proposed several relatively independent intelligences (linguistic, logical-mathematical, spatial, musical, bodily-kinaesthetic, interpersonal, intrapersonal). Spearman: g factor; Binet: first intelligence test; Cattell: fluid vs crystallised.

concept: Indoctrination instils unquestionable beliefs; anti-educational
must_teach: Indoctrination implants beliefs as unquestionable and discourages critical examination. Instruction delivers structured content, training builds skills by practice, tutoring gives individual help; these allow questioning.

concept: Positive classroom climate: mutual respect and open communication
must_teach: A positive climate shows mutual respect, warmth, open communication and shared purpose where students feel safe to err. Fear, public ranking/constant competition and minimal interaction raise anxiety and harm learning.

concept: Cone of Experience proposed by Edgar Dale (1946)
must_teach: Edgar Dale (1946) arranged learning experiences in a cone from direct purposeful experience (base) to verbal symbols (top); concrete supports abstract and guides choice of aids.

concept: Handling apparatus is a psychomotor objective
must_teach: Physical skills needing mind-muscle coordination, like handling apparatus, are psychomotor. Cognitive is thinking, affective is attitudes/values, conative is will or striving.

concept: Prior knowledge is a learner-related factor
must_teach: Learner factors include prior knowledge, which shapes reception of new material. Subject mastery is a teacher factor, library is an institutional facility, seating layout is learning environment.

concept: Bloom's cognitive domain covers intellectual abilities and thinking
must_teach: Cognitive domain covers knowing and thinking from recall to judgement; attitudes/feelings/values are affective; motor skills are psychomotor.

concept: Individual differences: learners differ in ability, interest, pace
must_teach: Individual differences means learners vary in intelligence, aptitude, interests, motivation, background and learning speed, which is why teachers vary methods and pace.

concept: Micro-teaching trains teachers in specific teaching skills
must_teach: Micro-teaching is a scaled-down teaching encounter in teacher training: short lesson (5-10 min) to a small group, one skill at a time, feedback, re-teach. It is unrelated to pupils' age or miniature models.

concept: Erikson: adolescence crisis is identity vs role confusion
must_teach: Erikson's adolescent stage is identity vs role confusion. Trust vs mistrust is infancy, industry vs inferiority school age, integrity vs despair old age.

concept: Flipped classroom: new content studied at home first
must_teach: In a flipped classroom students study new material before class via videos or readings; class time is used for discussion, problem-solving and application.

concept: Formative evaluation occurs during instruction for feedback
must_teach: Formative evaluation happens while teaching is in progress to give feedback and improve learning, not to grade. Summative is at the end; placement is before instruction; external is by outside examiners.

concept: Intrinsic motivation arises from learner's own interest
must_teach: Intrinsic motivation comes from within (interest, curiosity, satisfaction in the task); extrinsic depends on marks, prizes, praise or fear of punishment.

concept: Teaching is an intentional activity aimed at bringing about learning
must_teach: Teaching is a purposeful, planned activity to produce learning in another person; it is not accidental and is not defined by finishing the syllabus or maintaining discipline.

concept: Reflective level is the highest level of teaching
must_teach: Three levels in rising order: memory, understanding, reflective; reflective is highest and includes the lower two. 'Autonomous development level' is not one of the standard levels.

concept: Panel discussion: experts converse before audience with moderator
must_teach: In a panel discussion a few experts discuss among themselves before an audience, guided by a moderator. Tutorial = small-group guidance; workshop = hands-on practice; demonstration = showing how something is done.

concept: SWAYAM PRABHA delivers content via DTH television channels
must_teach: SWAYAM PRABHA is a group of DTH television channels telecasting educational programmes 24x7 for learners without internet; distinct from SWAYAM, the web MOOC platform.

concept: Evaluation includes value judgement; measurement only quantifies
must_teach: Measurement quantifies (e.g., 72/100); testing and scoring obtain that number. Evaluation judges the worth of performance against objectives and is the broadest term.

concept: Jackson's pre-active phase is lesson planning
must_teach: Philip Jackson's phases: pre-active (planning objectives, content, methods), interactive (classroom encounter), post-active (evaluation and reflection). 'Reactive phase' is not one.

concept: Rubric is a scoring guide with criteria and performance levels
must_teach: A rubric lists criteria and describes performance at each level (excellent, good, fair, poor), making marking transparent and consistent. It is not a question bank, timetable or marks register.

concept: CBCS stands for Choice Based Credit System
must_teach: CBCS = Choice Based Credit System (UGC guidelines 2015): students choose among core, elective and ability enhancement courses; credits, letter grades, grade points, CGPA.
flag: DATED: cites UGC CBCS guidelines of 2015; guide should note later CCFUP 2022/NEP frameworks — verify current framing.

concept: Chalkboard is a traditional teaching aid
must_teach: Chalkboard is the oldest traditional aid needing no electricity or device. Smart boards, webinar tools and learning apps are ICT-based. Support systems grouped as traditional, modern (audio-visual), ICT-based.

concept: Piaget's stage theory is of cognitive development
must_teach: Piaget's four cognitive stages: sensorimotor, pre-operational, concrete operational, formal operational (abstract reasoning from ~11-12). Psychosocial = Erikson; operant conditioning = Skinner; multiple intelligences = Gardner.

concept: SWAYAM is India's national MOOC platform
must_teach: SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds) is the MoE platform for free online courses (school to PG). Theses go to Shodhganga; plagiarism detection via ShodhShuddhi; rankings via NIRF.
flag: DATED: names ShodhShuddhi as plagiarism-detection service; verify current status/tool of INFLIBNET's scheme.

concept: Operant conditioning developed by B. F. Skinner
must_teach: Skinner: behaviour shaped by consequences; reinforced responses repeat (operant conditioning); programmed instruction applies it. Pavlov = classical conditioning; Köhler = insight; Bandura = observational learning.

concept: Pygmalion effect: teacher expectations influence student performance
must_teach: Rosenthal and Jacobson (1968) showed pupils expected to bloom gained more; the Pygmalion effect is a self-fulfilling prophecy of teacher expectations.

concept: Memory level of teaching associated with Herbart
must_teach: Herbart is the exponent of memory-level teaching; Morrison of understanding level; Hunt of reflective level. Bloom is known for the taxonomy, not a level.

concept: 'Learning by doing' associated with John Dewey
must_teach: John Dewey, progressive education, held that learners learn through active experience and reflection; basis of project and problem-solving methods. Herbart, Pavlov, Spearman are unrelated.

concept: In learner-centred approach teacher is facilitator
must_teach: In learner-centred teaching students are active and the teacher arranges conditions, guides and supports as facilitator; teacher as transmitter of information is typical of teacher-centred approach.

concept: Bloom 1956 lowest cognitive level is Knowledge
must_teach: Original order: Knowledge, Comprehension, Application, Analysis, Synthesis, Evaluation; Knowledge (recall) is lowest, renamed Remember in 2001.

concept: Memory level concerns rote learning and recall of facts
must_teach: Memory-level teaching focuses on committing facts to memory and reproducing them; teacher active, learner passive; lowest of the three levels (memory, understanding, reflective).

concept: Portfolio is a purposeful collection of student work over time
must_teach: A portfolio gathers samples of a student's work (drafts, projects, reflections) over time to show growth and process; an innovation supplementing written exams.

concept: Learner is the dependent variable in teaching
must_teach: Teacher = independent variable; learner = dependent variable whose behaviour changes; content, methods and strategies = intervening variables.

concept: Lowest level of affective domain is Receiving
must_teach: Krathwohl's affective levels in order: Receiving, Responding, Valuing, Organisation, Characterisation; Receiving (willingness to attend) is lowest.

concept: Scaffolding is temporary support withdrawn as learner gains competence
must_teach: Scaffolding is help (hints, prompts, models, questions) from teacher or capable peer to do a task just beyond current ability, removed gradually as the learner becomes independent.

concept: Objectivity: scores unaffected by examiner's personal judgement
must_teach: Objectivity means different examiners (or same examiner at different times) give the same score; MCQs highly objective, essays less. Objectivity supports reliability. Validity = measures what it claims.

concept: NPTEL is a joint initiative of IITs and IISc
must_teach: NPTEL (National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning) started 2003 by seven IITs and IISc with government funding; free online courses with optional proctored certificate exams.

concept: Gifted learners show exceptionally high ability
must_teach: Gifted learners perform far above their age group and need enrichment and challenge; slow learners need more time, repetition and concrete examples.

concept: Measurement is quantitative
must_teach: Measurement assigns numbers by rules and answers 'how much'; it does not judge worth. Judgement, which may use qualitative information, belongs to evaluation.

concept: Communication skill is a teacher-related factor
must_teach: Six factor groups: teacher, learner, support material, instructional facilities, learning environment, institution. Communication skill, subject mastery, personality are teacher factors; home background is learner; timetable is institutional.

concept: Understanding level propounded by H. C. Morrison
must_teach: Morrison's understanding-level model has five steps: exploration, presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation; aim is mastery of units. Thorndike and Skinner are learning theorists; Dale proposed the Cone of Experience.

concept: Blended learning combines face-to-face and online learning
must_teach: Blended (hybrid) learning is a planned mix of classroom teaching and online activities, giving online flexibility and in-class interaction.

concept: Seminar: paper presented then discussed
must_teach: In a seminar a student or scholar presents a prepared paper, then the group discusses and questions it under a chairperson. Supervised skill practice describes a workshop.

concept: Instructional objectives stated as observable learner behaviour
must_teach: An instructional objective states what the learner will be able to do after instruction in observable, assessable terms (define, explain, solve), not teacher activities, syllabus topics or lesson time.

concept: Micro-teaching practises one skill at a time
must_teach: Micro-teaching breaks teaching into component skills (questioning, explaining, reinforcement); trainee practises one skill per short lesson, gets feedback and re-teaches; skills are later integrated.

concept: Ultimate aim of teaching: desirable changes in learner behaviour
must_teach: Learning is relatively permanent change in behaviour; teaching aims to produce desirable change in knowledge, skills and attitudes. Syllabus coverage, marks and order are means or by-products.

concept: Good teaching is planned and purposeful
must_teach: Good teaching has clear objectives and organised plans, encourages interaction and questions, and respects learner differences; teacher-talk dominance, uniform treatment and discouraging questions are features of poor teaching.

concept: Levels order: memory, understanding, reflective
must_teach: Levels from lowest to highest are memory, understanding, reflective; each higher level presupposes the lower ones.

concept: Piaget's first stage is sensorimotor
must_teach: Piaget's stages: sensorimotor (0-2), pre-operational (2-7), concrete operational (7-11), formal operational (11+).

concept: Summative evaluation at end of course or term
must_teach: Summative evaluation sums up achievement after a unit/term/course, used for grading, promotion and certification. During lessons = formative; before instruction = placement or diagnostic.

concept: Hierarchy of needs given by Abraham Maslow
must_teach: Maslow's hierarchy: physiological, safety, love/belonging, esteem, self-actualisation; lower needs must be met first. Herzberg (two-factor), McClelland (achievement need), Rogers (humanistic facilitation) are others.

concept: SWAYAM is an initiative of the Ministry of Education
must_teach: SWAYAM was launched by the Ministry of Education (formerly MHRD); national coordinators include NPTEL, UGC, CEC, IGNOU, NCERT, NIOS (also AICTE, IIMB, NITTTR).

concept: MCQ, true-false, matching are objective-type items
must_teach: Objective-type items have one predetermined correct answer, sample widely and are quick to score; essay-type items need extended answers marked by judgement.

concept: Individual differences caused by heredity and environment together
must_teach: Individual differences arise from the interaction of heredity and environment (family, culture, schooling, health, opportunity); neither alone explains them.

concept: Open-book exam allows consulting books and notes
must_teach: In an open-book examination candidates may refer to books/notes, so good questions test understanding, application and analysis rather than memory; an evaluation innovation.

concept: Placement test assigns students to suitable levels before instruction
must_teach: Placement evaluation is done before instruction to determine entry level and grouping; summative and terminal tests come at the end; retention tests measure what is retained later.

concept: CBT stands for Computer Based Test
must_teach: In a computer-based test questions appear on screen, answers are marked by mouse/keyboard at a centre, and scored electronically; NTA uses this mode for national exams.

concept: Project method based on learning by doing
must_teach: The project method has students carry out a purposeful real-life task from planning to completion, reflecting Dewey's pragmatism and learning by doing; it replaces rote and passive listening.

concept: Discovery learning associated with Jerome Bruner
must_teach: Bruner held learners understand best what they discover themselves. Ausubel = meaningful reception learning; Gagné = conditions of learning; Bandura = observational learning.

concept: Revised taxonomy renamed Knowledge as Remember
must_teach: Revised taxonomy turned nouns into verbs: Knowledge became Remember, Comprehension became Understand, etc.; Synthesis became Create and moved above Evaluate. Recall and recognise are processes under Remember, not level names.

concept: Classical conditioning demonstrated by Ivan Pavlov
must_teach: Pavlov paired a bell with food until the bell alone elicited salivation (classical conditioning). Skinner = operant; Thorndike = trial and error; Lewin = field theory/leadership.

concept: Validity: test measures what it intends to measure
must_teach: Validity, the most important test quality, is whether a test measures what it claims; reliability is consistency, objectivity is freedom from scorer bias, practicability is usability.

concept: General intelligence factor 'g' proposed by Spearman
must_teach: Spearman's two-factor theory: general factor g plus specific factor s. Gardner, Sternberg and Guilford rejected intelligence as a single ability.

concept: Maxim: from simple to complex
must_teach: Accepted maxims: simple to complex, known to unknown, concrete to abstract, particular to general (also whole to part, induction to deduction, empirical to rational). Reversed forms are wrong.

concept: SGPA means Semester Grade Point Average
must_teach: SGPA = total credit points (credits x grade points) in a semester divided by total credits of that semester; CGPA does the same across all semesters.

concept: Training develops specific skills through repeated practice
must_teach: Training aims at skill proficiency through practice and drill; instruction imparts structured knowledge; indoctrination implants unquestioned beliefs; counselling helps with personal/academic problems.

concept: Demonstration method suits practical skills and procedures
must_teach: In demonstration the teacher shows step by step how something is done while explaining (lab experiment, instrument use), so it suits practical skills and procedures.

concept: Pedagogy is the art and science of teaching children
must_teach: Pedagogy, from Greek 'leading the child', is teaching children with teacher-directed learning; andragogy is helping adults learn.

concept: Reflective level is organised around a problem
must_teach: Reflective-level teaching is problem-centred: teacher creates a problematic situation; learners examine critically, form and test hypotheses, reach conclusions. Memorising/reciting belong to memory level.

concept: Cooperative learning: small groups toward shared goal
must_teach: Cooperative learning places students in small mixed groups with individual and group responsibility for a shared goal, developing academic and social skills; opposite of individual competition or solitary work.

concept: Academic calendar and timetable are institution-related factors
must_teach: Institution-related factors include academic calendar, timetable, workload, class size, rules and administrative support, which set limits on teacher planning.

concept: Comprehension follows Knowledge in Bloom's original taxonomy
must_teach: Original order: Knowledge, Comprehension, Application, Analysis, Synthesis, Evaluation; Comprehension means grasping meaning (explain, summarise).

concept: ICT means Information and Communication Technology
must_teach: ICT = Information and Communication Technology: digital tools to create, store, send and receive information (computers, internet, projectors, mobiles, software).

concept: Criterion-referenced test compares with fixed mastery standard
must_teach: Criterion-referenced tests check whether a pre-set standard is reached (e.g., driving test), irrespective of others; norm-referenced compares students with one another.

concept: Role play: learners act out parts of persons in a situation
must_teach: In role play learners take the parts of people in a real or imagined situation and act it out unscripted, followed by discussion; builds empathy and social skills.

concept: Core course is compulsory in CBCS
must_teach: Under CBCS, core courses are compulsory; electives are chosen from a pool (discipline-specific or generic); ability enhancement courses build general skills; each course carries credits.

concept: Adolescence as 'storm and stress' (G. Stanley Hall)
must_teach: G. Stanley Hall described adolescence as a period of storm and stress due to rapid growth, emotional swings, identity search and conflict with authority.

concept: At memory level the learner is a passive receiver
must_teach: Memory-level teaching is teacher-dominated; learner receives, retains, reproduces. Active inquiry and independent criticism belong to the reflective level.

concept: Socialisation as a function of teaching
must_teach: Functions of teaching include transmitting knowledge, developing skills, inculcating values and socialisation, i.e., helping learners adjust to societal norms; certification and examination are system outcomes.

concept: Clear communication is a basic requirement of teaching
must_teach: Basic requirements of teaching include clear communication, subject knowledge, planning and understanding learners; costly equipment is not essential; silence or unbroken lecture means no interaction.

concept: Lighting, ventilation, seating are physical environment
must_teach: Learning environment has a physical side (space, light, air, furniture, noise) and a psychological side (relationships, warmth, freedom from fear).

concept: Overhead projector projects transparencies
must_teach: OHP projects an enlarged image of a transparent sheet onto a screen while the teacher faces the class; a projected visual aid now largely replaced by LCD projectors.

concept: Programmed instruction based on Skinner's operant conditioning
must_teach: Programmed instruction breaks content into small frames, requires active response, gives immediate confirmation (reinforcement) and allows self-pacing; it applies Skinner's operant conditioning.

concept: Percentile ranks interpret scores in norm-referenced tests
must_teach: A percentile rank gives the percentage of the group scoring below a student, i.e., relative position, which is norm-referenced interpretation. Criterion-referenced and mastery tests report whether a fixed standard is reached.

concept: Teacher dominance greatest at memory level
must_teach: Teacher control is greatest at memory level, less at understanding level, least at reflective level where learners investigate and the teacher guides.

concept: 'Massive' in MOOC means very large number of enrolled learners
must_teach: MOOC = Massive Open Online Course: 'massive' means unlimited/large enrolment, 'open' means anyone can join usually free without entry qualification; courses usually last a few weeks.

concept: IQ means Intelligence Quotient (MA/CA x 100)
must_teach: IQ = mental age / chronological age x 100 (Stern's idea, used by Terman); 100 is average; modern tests use deviation IQ.

concept: LMS means Learning Management System
must_teach: An LMS is software to deliver and manage online courses (materials, assignments, quizzes, forums, grades); examples Moodle, Google Classroom, Canvas, Blackboard.

concept: Drill and repetition typical of memory level
must_teach: Memory-level teaching uses telling, drill, repetition, recitation and review; debate, projects, seminars require understanding/reflection and belong to higher levels.

concept: Scope order: measurement, assessment, evaluation
must_teach: Measurement assigns numbers; assessment gathers and interprets numerical and descriptive information about learning; evaluation judges worth. From narrowest to broadest: measurement, assessment, evaluation.

concept: Understanding level: learner explains ideas in own words
must_teach: Understanding shows when learners restate ideas, give examples, see relationships and apply principles in familiar situations. Exact repetition is memory level; independent discovery is reflective level.

concept: Good teaching involves two-way communication
must_teach: Good teaching is interactive: teacher explains and asks, learners respond and question, teacher adjusts through feedback; one-way talk gives no feedback on understanding.

concept: Classroom encounter is Jackson's interactive phase
must_teach: Interactive phase covers everything from entering class to lesson end (presenting, questioning, responding, reinforcing); planning = pre-active; evaluation afterwards = post-active.

concept: Verb 'define' belongs to Remember level
must_teach: Action verbs: Remember (define, list, name, state, recall); Apply (solve, use); Analyse (compare, differentiate); Create (design, compose).

concept: Find learners' previous knowledge (entry behaviour) before planning
must_teach: New learning must link to what learners already know; previous knowledge or entry behaviour tells the teacher where to begin and which examples to use.

concept: Workshop is for hands-on practice of skills
must_teach: A workshop is a working session where participants learn by doing, practising a skill or producing something with guidance from resource persons. Paper reading = seminar; expert debate = panel/symposium.

concept: 'Preparing Instructional Objectives' by Robert Mager (1962)
must_teach: Mager's 1962 book taught writing behavioural objectives with three parts: performance, conditions, criterion. Bloom = taxonomy; Tyler = curriculum principles; Gagné = conditions of learning.

concept: Conditioning works through stimulus-response association
must_teach: Conditioning builds a fixed stimulus-response connection by pairing or reinforcement (Pavlov, Skinner), without requiring understanding; it sits at the lowest end of the conditioning-training-instruction-teaching continuum.

concept: Case study method popularised by Harvard Business School
must_teach: The case method was developed at Harvard, first in law, then from the 1920s at Harvard Business School, where students analyse real business situations and propose decisions.

concept: Class quiz is a formative evaluation tool
must_teach: A class quiz given during teaching shows what has been learnt and what needs work (formative). Year-end exams and degree viva are summative; entrance exams are for selection.

concept: Reflective level associated with Hunt (and Bigge)
must_teach: Reflective-level teaching model is linked with Hunt and discussed by Bigge; problem-centred, aiming at critical independent thinking. Herbart = memory level; Pavlov and Thorndike are learning theorists.
flag: DOUBT: attribution variously given as Hunt, Bigge, or Bigge and Hunt; guide should present both names.

concept: Vygotsky stresses social interaction (social constructivism)
must_teach: For Vygotsky learning is first social then individual, through interaction with adults and capable peers with language as chief tool (social constructivism). Reinforcement and trial and error are behaviourist.

concept: CBCS introduced through UGC guidelines (2015)
must_teach: UGC issued CBCS guidelines in 2015 for a common credit and grading pattern. NCERT handles school education, NCTE teacher education, NAAC accreditation.

concept: Self-actualisation is highest in Maslow's hierarchy
must_teach: Maslow's top need is self-actualisation (realising full potential), above physiological, safety, belonging and esteem.

concept: Teacher warmth and enthusiasm motivate learners
must_teach: A warm, enthusiastic teacher arouses interest and effort and builds trust; personality is a teacher-related factor along with subject mastery and communication skill.

concept: Characterisation: values become consistent way of life
must_teach: Affective levels: Receiving, Responding, Valuing, Organisation, Characterisation by a value or value complex; at Characterisation values form a consistent philosophy governing behaviour.

concept: Slow learners need more time and repeated practice
must_teach: Slow learners need slower pace, simple language, concrete examples, repetition, frequent encouragement and peer tutoring; speeding up or withholding feedback widens the gap.

concept: Radio is an audio aid
must_teach: Aids classified by sense: audio (radio, tape recorder, podcast), visual (charts, models, globes), audio-visual (television, films).

concept: Noise distracts learners' attention (physical barrier)
must_teach: Noise is a physical barrier in the learning environment that competes for attention; it does not change intelligence or aptitude, which are stable learner traits.

concept: Peer assessment: students judge classmates' work against criteria
must_teach: In peer assessment students give feedback/marks on classmates' work, usually with a rubric; in self-assessment students judge their own work; both are evaluation innovations.

concept: Law of effect formulated by Thorndike
must_teach: Thorndike's law of effect: satisfying results strengthen a response, annoying ones weaken it; with laws of readiness and exercise forms trial-and-error learning (connectionism). Pavlov = classical; Köhler and Koffka = Gestalt/insight.

concept: Adults prefer problem-centred, life-relevant learning
must_teach: Knowles: adults need to know why they learn and want immediate application, so prefer problem-centred learning; subject-centred learning for later use is typical of pedagogy.

concept: CBT advantage: quick scoring and results
must_teach: CBT records responses electronically for near-instant error-free scoring; it still needs test centres, identity verification and reliable equipment; technical failure and unequal computer familiarity are limitations.

concept: Essay-type item requires long organised written answer
must_teach: Essay items let students organise and express ideas, testing higher abilities, but have limited sampling and subjective scoring; matching, completion and true-false are objective-type.

concept: LCD projector displays computer output on large screen
must_teach: An LCD/LED projector connected to a computer displays slides, video and web pages for the class; printers make paper copies, scanners digitise paper, webcams capture video.

concept: Peer group is strongest social influence in adolescence
must_teach: Adolescents seek acceptance from peers; peer norms shape dress, speech, interests and study attitudes; teachers can use group work and peer learning constructively.

concept: Synthesis: putting parts together to form new whole
must_teach: Synthesis (fifth original level) combines elements into a new pattern or structure; Analysis breaks a whole into parts; Application uses learning in new situations; Comprehension grasps meaning.

concept: Flipped class time used for discussion and problem-solving
must_teach: Since content is studied at home, flipped class time is used for clearing doubts, discussion, problem-solving and application; the lecture moves out in recorded form.

concept: Usability means practicability of a test (time, cost, ease)
must_teach: Qualities of a good test: validity, reliability, objectivity, usability; usability/practicability means the test can be given, scored and interpreted without undue time, cost or difficulty.

concept: Lecture covers much content for many learners quickly
must_teach: Lecture's main advantage is economy: much organised content to a large class quickly; weaknesses are little activity, little interaction and no adjustment to individual pace.

concept: Concrete to abstract: start with real objects and examples
must_teach: Maxim 'concrete to abstract' means beginning with things learners can see, handle or picture before definitions, rules and theories, which are abstract.

concept: Revised taxonomy levels are expressed as verbs
must_teach: Original taxonomy used nouns (Knowledge, Comprehension, Application...); the 2001 revision uses verbs (Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create).

concept: Cater to individual differences by varying methods and pace
must_teach: To meet individual differences teachers vary methods and pace, give graded tasks and extra help or enrichment (differentiated instruction); one fixed method or common task suits few.

concept: Gage defined teaching as interpersonal influence changing behaviour potential
must_teach: N. L. Gage (1963): teaching is a form of interpersonal influence aimed at changing the behaviour potential of another person; involves two persons and intention to change behaviour.

concept: Advance organisers given by David Ausubel
must_teach: Ausubel proposed advance organisers, brief general introductions presented before detailed content to give a framework, central to meaningful verbal learning. Bruner = discovery; Gagné = conditions of learning; Bandura = observational learning.

concept: Content validity: test covers syllabus in proportion (via blueprint)
must_teach: Content validity is how well items represent course content and objectives, ensured by a blueprint distributing marks over topics and objectives. Predictive validity forecasts future performance; retest reliability is consistency over time.

concept: In brainstorming criticism is deferred
must_teach: Osborn's rules: defer judgement, welcome unusual ideas, aim at quantity, build on others' ideas; evaluation is a separate later stage.

concept: Board of Studies frames the syllabus
must_teach: The Board of Studies (teachers plus external experts) frames and revises the syllabus, which goes to the Academic Council for approval; finance, building and selection committees have other roles.

concept: Group discussion is a learner-centred method
must_teach: In group discussion learners do most talking and thinking with teacher guidance (learner-centred); lecture, dictation and teacher demonstration are teacher-centred.

concept: Micro-teaching lesson lasts about 5-10 minutes
must_teach: Micro-teaching scales down class (5-10 pupils), time (5-10 minutes) and task (one skill); a normal period is 40-45 minutes.

concept: Abstract hypothetical thinking develops in formal operational stage
must_teach: From about 11-12 years (formal operational) young people reason about possibilities and hypotheses; concrete operational thinking is tied to real objects.

concept: Interest is an affective learner factor
must_teach: Learner characteristics are cognitive (intelligence, aptitude, previous knowledge), affective (interest, attitude, motivation, values) and psychomotor; interest is affective.

concept: First step of problem-solving method is identifying the problem
must_teach: Problem-solving steps: recognise/define problem, collect data, form hypotheses, test them, draw conclusion.

concept: Analysis: breaking material into parts and finding relationships
must_teach: Analysis (fourth original level) separates a whole into elements and finds relations (e.g., facts vs opinions); Synthesis combines parts into a new whole; Evaluation judges worth against criteria; Comprehension grasps meaning.

concept: Professional competence = subject knowledge plus pedagogical skill
must_teach: Teacher competence consists of knowing the subject and how to teach it (planning, explaining, questioning, managing class, assessing); seniority, appearance and administrative post do not improve learning.

concept: Willing participation is the Responding level
must_teach: Receiving = merely attending; Responding = reacting actively and willingly (answering, participating, volunteering); Valuing = attaching worth and showing commitment; Organisation = building a value system.

concept: Wrong options in an MCQ are distractors
must_teach: An MCQ has a stem (the problem), a key (correct option) and distractors (plausible wrong options). Premises and responses are the columns of a matching item.

concept: Bruner's modes: enactive, iconic, symbolic
must_teach: Bruner's modes of representation: enactive (action), iconic (images), symbolic (language/symbols), usually taught in that order. VAK are learning styles; receiving/responding/valuing are affective levels; preparation/presentation/application are Herbartian steps.

concept: Models are three-dimensional aids
must_teach: Three-dimensional aids (models, specimens, objects, globes, mock-ups) have length, breadth and depth; charts, maps and photographs are two-dimensional. Models help when the real object is too big, small or costly.

concept: e-PG Pathshala provides e-content for postgraduate courses
must_teach: e-PG Pathshala is a UGC initiative under NME-ICT providing curriculum-based interactive e-content for PG subjects. NCERT's ePathshala has school textbooks; Virtual Labs has simulated experiments; plagiarism software is separate.

concept: Set induction links new topic to previous knowledge at lesson start
must_teach: Set induction (introducing a lesson) arouses interest and connects topic with prior knowledge; closure consolidates at the end; stimulus variation holds attention; reinforcement encourages desired responses.

concept: Shuffling question order in CBT reduces copying
must_teach: In CBT, randomising questions and options (from a question bank) means neighbours don't see the same item in the same position, a security advantage over a single printed paper.

concept: Recall tests suit memory-level outcomes
must_teach: Memory-level evaluation uses recall and recognition (objective) items; understanding level needs explanation/application items; reflective level uses essay-type and open-ended tasks.

concept: Reporting a score without judgement is measurement
must_teach: A plain quantity ('68 out of 100') is measurement; adding a value judgement ('good for his class') makes it evaluation; appraisal is another word for judgement.

concept: Flipped classroom popularised by Bergmann and Sams
must_teach: Jonathan Bergmann and Aaron Sams, US chemistry teachers, began recording lectures in 2007 (book Flip Your Classroom). Hase and Kenyon = heutagogy; Siemens and Downes = connectivism; Joyce and Weil = models of teaching.

concept: Herbartian steps include Preparation
must_teach: Herbartian steps (memory level): preparation, presentation, comparison/association, generalisation, application. Exploration, assimilation, organisation, recitation (with presentation) are Morrison's understanding-level steps.

concept: Authentic assessment uses real-life tasks
must_teach: Authentic assessment has learners apply knowledge in tasks resembling real life or work (case analyses, projects, presentations, reports for real audiences), revealing what recall tests miss.

concept: Emotional intelligence popularised by Daniel Goleman (1995)
must_teach: EI was introduced by Salovey and Mayer and popularised by Goleman's Emotional Intelligence (1995): self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy, social skills. Gardner's inter/intrapersonal intelligences are a different theory; Thurstone = primary mental abilities; Binet = first IQ test.

concept: Assimilation fits new information into existing schema
must_teach: Piaget: assimilation interprets new experience via an existing schema; accommodation changes the schema; equilibration balances the two; conservation is a concrete-operational achievement.

concept: Inductive method proceeds from examples to rule
must_teach: Inductive method: learners examine particular examples and derive the general rule (suits discovery). Deductive method states rule/definition first then applies to examples (saves time).

concept: RPwD Act enacted 2016; 21 disabilities
must_teach: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 replaced the PwD Act 1995, raised recognised disabilities from 7 to 21, and requires inclusive education and reasonable accommodation. RTE Act is 2009.

concept: Project method steps: purposing, planning, executing, evaluating
must_teach: Kilpatrick's four steps in order: purposing (choose a purposeful project), planning, executing, evaluating/judging against the original purpose.

concept: OER are freely available for use and adaptation
must_teach: Open Educational Resources are materials in any medium in the public domain or under open licence that anyone may use, adapt and redistribute free (open courseware, open textbooks, many SWAYAM materials).

concept: Symposium: several speakers present different aspects of a topic
must_teach: A symposium is a series of short prepared talks by different speakers on aspects of one theme, followed by audience questions. Distinguish from lecture, role play and micro-teaching.

concept: SWAYAM courses free; fee only for certification exam
must_teach: Anyone may enrol in SWAYAM courses free; a fee is paid only for certification via a proctored exam; credits earned can be transferred to the learner's university.
flag: DATED: certification fee and credit-transfer rules (UGC SWAYAM regulations) change; verify current position.

concept: A credit indicates course weightage in teaching hours
must_teach: Under UGC CBCS, one credit generally = one hour lecture/tutorial or two hours practical per week through a semester; credits show relative weight of courses and are used in GPA calculation.
flag: DATED: credit-hour equivalence stated per CBCS 2015; UGC CCFUP 2022/NCrF express credits as 15 contact hours (30 for practicals) per semester — guide should present current norm.

concept: Morrison's model begins with exploration
must_teach: Morrison's five steps: exploration (finding what learners already know), presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation.

concept: Studying for a scholarship is extrinsic motivation
must_teach: Working for a reward outside the activity (scholarship) is extrinsic motivation; studying because the subject is interesting is intrinsic; external rewards overused can weaken interest.

concept: Simulation: practice in an artificial situation resembling reality
must_teach: Simulation lets learners practise under conditions resembling reality (mock court, flight simulator, simulated teaching) where mistakes carry no real cost. Working in a real workplace is apprenticeship/internship, not simulation.

concept: Class size and teaching workload decided by institution
must_teach: Admissions, sections, class size, timetable and teaching load are fixed by institutional policy; examples, questions and tone of voice are the teacher's choices.

concept: Lecture limitation: learners remain largely passive
must_teach: Lecture communication is mostly one-way so learners listen passively with little questioning or application; attention falls after 15-20 minutes. Syllabus coverage, handling large classes and introducing topics are strengths.

concept: Good teaching is flexible and adaptive
must_teach: A good teacher reads class feedback and changes pace, example or method; flexibility is a characteristic of effective teaching.

concept: Aptitude is potential to acquire a skill with training
must_teach: Aptitude is future-oriented potential to learn with training; achievement is what has been learnt; interest is liking for an activity; attitude is a settled tendency to respond favourably or unfavourably.

concept: Letter grades reduce over-fine distinctions among students
must_teach: Small mark differences are within measurement error; grades place students in broad bands, reducing misclassification, unhealthy competition and stress; examinations are still needed.

concept: Starting from students' own experience is 'known to unknown'
must_teach: Linking new material (democracy) to what students already know (class elections) follows 'from known to unknown'; it moves from particular case, so 'general to particular' does not fit.

concept: Knowles: adult learners are self-directed
must_teach: Knowles' assumptions: adults move from dependence to self-direction, use experience as a resource, are ready to learn for their roles, prefer problem-centred learning, are internally motivated.

concept: Predictive validity: scores forecast later success
must_teach: Predictive validity (a criterion-related validity) is how well scores foretell later performance, essential for entrance/aptitude tests. Content validity = syllabus coverage; face validity = looks appropriate; internal consistency is a reliability measure.

concept: Revised taxonomy order: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse
must_teach: Revised levels in order: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create.

concept: Vygotsky's More Knowledgeable Other
must_teach: The More Knowledgeable Other (teacher, parent, capable peer or tool) supports the learner within the ZPD. 'Generalised other' is G. H. Mead's term; advance organiser is Ausubel's.

concept: Reflective level develops critical and creative thinking
must_teach: At reflective level learners face problems, question assumptions, weigh evidence and produce solutions, developing critical and creative thinking and independence; memorisation, imitation and listening suffice only for lower levels.

concept: Prescriptive function selects remedial methods and strategies
must_teach: Three functions of teaching: diagnostic (finding entry behaviour and difficulties), prescriptive (selecting content, methods, strategies), evaluative (checking achievement of objectives).

concept: Micro-teaching class size is 5-10 pupils
must_teach: Micro-teaching reduces class to about 5-10 pupils (real pupils or peers), with a short lesson and single skill.

concept: Thorndike's theory is trial and error learning
must_teach: Thorndike's puzzle-box cats learned by trial and error, stamping in correct S-R connections (connectionism). Insight = Köhler; classical conditioning = Pavlov; social learning = Bandura.

concept: Teaching is widest concept including instruction and training
must_teach: Continuum: conditioning, training, instruction, teaching; each later term is wider. Training shapes skills, instruction imparts knowledge, teaching covers both plus understanding, attitudes and values.

concept: Driving test is criterion-referenced
must_teach: A test where everyone meeting a fixed standard passes, regardless of others, is criterion-referenced; in norm-referenced tests success is limited by rank (competitive exams for fixed seats).

concept: Think-Pair-Share (Lyman) is a cooperative learning technique
must_teach: Think-Pair-Share, devised by Frank Lyman: think alone, discuss with a partner, share with class; a cooperative learning technique enabling participation in large classes.

concept: Split-half method estimates reliability
must_teach: Split-half: test given once, divided into halves (odd/even), scores correlated and corrected with Spearman-Brown formula to estimate reliability; other methods are test-retest and parallel forms.

concept: Hero-worship and day-dreaming typical of adolescence
must_teach: Adolescents idealise heroes (sports stars, leaders, teachers) and day-dream about future roles, linked to identity search and emotional intensity.

concept: Teaching aims at learning but learning can occur without teaching
must_teach: Teaching is intentional activity aimed at learning; the two are related but distinct processes; learning also occurs through experience and self-study without teaching.

concept: Summative results used for grading and certification
must_teach: Summative evaluation results are used for grades, promotion and certificates; daily feedback is formative; placement and diagnosis are separate types.

concept: CGPA calculated over all semesters
must_teach: CGPA is the credit-weighted average of grade points across all courses in all semesters; SGPA is for a single semester; both appear on the transcript.

concept: Criterion in a behavioural objective states how well learner must perform
must_teach: Mager's objective has performance (what learner does), conditions (circumstances/materials) and criterion (standard of acceptable performance, e.g., 8 of 10 correct).

concept: Circular or U-shaped seating supports discussion
must_teach: Seeing one another's faces encourages student-to-student talk, so circular/U-shaped seating suits discussion; rows and tiered halls focus attention to the front and suit lectures.

concept: Webinar is a seminar conducted over the internet
must_teach: Webinar = web + seminar: a live online session where a speaker presents to remote participants who ask questions via chat/audio; synchronous ICT mode. Not a recording, a listing website or a printed report.

concept: Formative and summative terms introduced by Michael Scriven (1967)
must_teach: Scriven introduced formative and summative in 1967 for curriculum evaluation; Bloom and colleagues applied them to student learning. Tyler = objectives-based evaluation; Glaser = criterion-referenced measurement; Mager = behavioural objectives.

concept: Using a learnt formula in a new problem is Application
must_teach: Application is using a learnt rule or method in a new concrete situation; stating it is Knowledge, explaining it is Comprehension, judging worth is Evaluation.

concept: Grading on a curve is norm-referenced
must_teach: Grading on a curve fixes in advance the proportion receiving each grade, so grades depend on relative standing (norm-referenced, relative grading); in criterion-referenced (absolute) grading everyone reaching the standard can get top grade.

concept: Showing whole map before states is 'whole to part'
must_teach: Maxim 'whole to part', based on Gestalt psychology: present the complete picture first, then details. Starting with parts and building up is the reverse; 'particular to general' and 'empirical to rational' are other maxims.

concept: CBT limitation: unequal access to and familiarity with computers
must_teach: In developing countries, the digital divide (rural/poor candidates less familiar with computers) and technical failures are CBT's chief limitations; objective scoring, speed and item shuffling are advantages.

concept: Intra-individual differences are differences within one person's abilities
must_teach: Intra-individual differences: variation among one person's own abilities (strong in language, weak in maths). Inter-individual differences: between persons.

concept: Self-assessment helps learners reflect on strengths and weaknesses
must_teach: Self-assessment against clear criteria makes learners aware of what they have and haven't mastered (metacognition) and supplements teacher feedback; it is not about ranking or avoiding feedback.

concept: Undergraduate entrants are in late adolescence
must_teach: Students join college at about 17-18, late adolescence: capable of abstract thought, forming identity, peer-influenced; PG and research students are mostly young adults.

concept: Lectures improved by questions and visual aids at intervals
must_teach: Lecture attention drops after about 15 minutes; breaking it with questions, examples, short activities and visual aids restores attention and makes it two-way; speaking fast, reading from the book or avoiding eye contact harm it.

concept: Feedback is not scaled down in micro-teaching
must_teach: Micro-teaching scales down class size, lesson length and number of skills, but feedback is central, immediate and detailed (supervisor, peers, video).

concept: Credit points = grade point x credits
must_teach: Credit points for a course = credits x grade point (e.g., 4 credits x GP 8 = 32); SGPA = sum of credit points / total credits in the semester.

concept: Maturation is natural growth that makes learning possible
must_teach: Maturation is the unfolding of physical and mental capacities with age, independent of training; learners must be mature enough (readiness) for teaching to succeed. Coaching, discipline and testing are external influences.

concept: Food and water are physiological needs (Maslow)
must_teach: Physiological needs (food, water, sleep, shelter) form Maslow's base, followed by safety, love/belonging, esteem, self-actualisation.

concept: 'Understand' corresponds to original 'Comprehension'
must_teach: Mapping: Knowledge to Remember, Comprehension to Understand, Application to Apply, Analysis to Analyse; Synthesis became Create and moved to top above Evaluate.

concept: A well-equipped laboratory is an instructional facility
must_teach: Instructional facilities are physical resources an institution provides (classrooms, labs, libraries, projectors, internet). Humour is a teacher trait, aptitude a learner trait, syllabus policy institutional.

concept: Test-retest method estimates reliability as stability
must_teach: Test-retest gives the same test twice and correlates scores (stability). Split-half and rational equivalence (Kuder-Richardson) use one administration (internal consistency); parallel forms use two equivalent versions.

concept: Memory level is prerequisite for the other two levels
must_teach: Understanding needs facts, and reflection needs facts and understanding, so memory level is the base for understanding and reflective levels. 'Insight level' is not a standard level.

concept: Instructional objectives are specific and short-term vs broad aims
must_teach: Aims are broad, long-term purposes (e.g., responsible citizens); instructional objectives are narrow, precise, achievable and testable at the end of a lesson or unit.

concept: Fear of asking questions indicates poor psychological climate
must_teach: Psychological/socio-emotional climate depends on relationships; fear of ridicule or punishment silences students even if room and curriculum are fine.

concept: Diagnostic testing is followed by remedial teaching
must_teach: Diagnosis locates specific weaknesses and causes so the teacher can plan remedial instruction; grading and certification follow summative evaluation.

concept: Hybrid learning is another name for blended learning
must_teach: Hybrid/blended learning combines classroom and online learning in one course. Distance learning separates teacher and learner; programmed learning uses frames; mastery learning requires mastery of each unit before the next.

concept: Memory-level limitation: facts without understanding are soon forgotten
must_teach: Rote-memorised material has few links, fades quickly and cannot be applied; memory level also leaves learners passive. Criticism and lengthy investigation belong to the reflective level.

concept: Adults' richest learning resource is life and work experience
must_teach: Knowles: adults bring large, varied experience; methods drawing on it (discussion, case studies, problem-solving) work better than one-way transmission.

concept: 'Open' in MOOC means anyone may enrol without entry requirements
must_teach: MOOCs are open: enrolment not restricted by qualification, institution or place, usually free; they still have instructors, a schedule of several weeks and assessments, with fee typically only for certificates.

concept: Consistently acting on a belief one holds worthwhile is Valuing
must_teach: Valuing means attaching worth and acting on it consistently; Receiving = attention; Responding = participation. Imitation is a psychomotor (Dave) level, not affective.

concept: Instruction: organised imparting of knowledge, closest to teaching
must_teach: Instruction is systematic imparting of knowledge (possible without a teacher, via programmed text or computer); it is part of teaching, which is wider. Conditioning, indoctrination and propaganda do not aim at understanding or free judgement.

concept: Three focal points: teacher, learner, subject matter
must_teach: Teaching brings together teacher, learner and subject matter (content); effective teaching attends to all three.
flag: DOUBT: tripolar process is often given as teacher-learner-curriculum (Bloom's tripolar: objectives, learning experiences, evaluation is a different triad); guide should distinguish the two tripolar notions.

concept: At reflective level teacher is a democratic guide
must_teach: At reflective level the teacher raises a problem, helps clarify it and supports inquiry without imposing conclusions; classroom is open and democratic, teacher neither authoritarian nor passive spectator.

concept: Teaching is a profession: specialised knowledge, training, code of ethics
must_teach: A profession is marked by specialised knowledge, long training, service motive and a code of conduct; salary, post and facilities are conditions of employment, not marks of a profession.

concept: Vygotsky: language is the chief tool of thought
must_teach: Vygotsky saw language as the chief cultural tool: social speech becomes private speech guiding action, then silent inner speech (thought).

concept: Guessing chance greatest in true-false items
must_teach: True-false items have two choices, so blind guessing gives 50% chance; four-option MCQ gives 25%; supply-type items (essay, short-answer, completion) leave little room for guessing.

concept: Case study: analyse realistic situation and propose solutions
must_teach: A case is an account of a real or realistic problem; students study facts, identify issues, discuss alternatives and defend a decision, linking theory and practice.

concept: Evaluation and reflection after lesson belong to post-active phase
must_teach: Post-active phase follows teaching: testing achievement of objectives, selecting testing devices, changing strategies; findings feed back into pre-active planning. 'Inactive phase' is not a phase.

concept: Democratic teaching respects students' views and invites questions
must_teach: Democratic teaching treats learners with respect, gives freedom to ask, differ and participate, and reasons rather than commands; it does not mean abdicating responsibilities or leaving errors uncorrected.

concept: Conservation: quantity unchanged despite change in appearance
must_teach: Conservation (concrete operational) is understanding quantity/number/mass stays same despite appearance change. Egocentrism and animism are pre-operational; object permanence develops in sensorimotor stage.

concept: Braille is for learners with visual impairment
must_teach: Braille is a raised-dot system read by touch for blind/low-vision learners; hearing-impaired learners use sign language and captions.

concept: Face validity: test appears on the surface to measure its target
must_teach: Face validity is the surface impression of relevance to candidates/lay observers, not technical validity; content, predictive and construct validity require systematic evidence.

concept: Dave's psychomotor taxonomy begins with Imitation
must_teach: Dave's five psychomotor levels: Imitation, Manipulation, Precision, Articulation, Naturalisation.

concept: Heuristic method advocated by H. E. Armstrong
must_teach: H. E. Armstrong advocated the heuristic method (Greek 'I find out') for science: pupils as discoverers with minimal telling. Kilpatrick = project method; Parkhurst = Dalton Plan; Montessori = early childhood method.

concept: Morrison's steps: exploration, presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation
must_teach: Morrison's order: exploration (prior knowledge), presentation, assimilation (supervised study), organisation (written without help), recitation (oral presentation to class).

concept: Brainstorming introduced by Alex Osborn
must_teach: Alex F. Osborn, advertising executive, described brainstorming in Applied Imagination. De Bono = lateral thinking/six hats; Guilford = structure of intellect/divergent thinking; Lyman = Think-Pair-Share.

concept: Reward after desired response is positive reinforcement
must_teach: Positive reinforcement adds something pleasant to strengthen a response; negative reinforcement removes something unpleasant to strengthen it; punishment weakens; extinction is fading when reinforcement stops.

concept: First practical intelligence test by Alfred Binet (1905)
must_teach: Binet with Simon produced the first workable intelligence scale in France in 1905, introducing mental age. Wechsler later built adult/child scales; Spearman = g; Cattell = fluid/crystallised.

concept: Flash cards suit quick drill of words and facts
must_teach: Flash cards carry a word, picture, formula or question shown briefly; suit drill, revision and recall; simple non-projected visual aids.

concept: Synchronous learning: teacher and students together in real time
must_teach: Synchronous learning happens live for all (live video class, webinar) with immediate interaction; asynchronous uses recorded lectures, forums and assignments at learners' convenience.

concept: Clarity of explanation depends on command of subject and language
must_teach: Clear explanation depends on subject mastery and communication/language skill (teacher factors); age, service length, status, handwriting and dress have no direct bearing.

concept: Small unit in programmed instruction is a frame
must_teach: A programme is a sequence of frames, each giving small information, requiring a response, with immediate check; principles: small steps, active responding, immediate confirmation, self-pacing.

concept: Ausubel's theory is meaningful verbal learning
must_teach: Ausubel: most classroom learning is reception of verbal material, meaningful when related to existing knowledge (contrasted with rote). Discovery = Bruner; operant = Skinner; observational = Bandura.

concept: Moderator conducts a panel discussion
must_teach: The moderator introduces topic and panel, puts questions, ensures fair turns, prevents digression and sums up; a rapporteur records proceedings and reports; an invigilator supervises exams.
